Mimas
bodies.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute/Lunar and Planetary Institute; mosaic by Paul Schenk (LPI)
bodies.limits: Static Cassini ISS global mosaic (PIA18437, 2014) in enhanced IR-green-UV colour, not natural colour or calibrated albedo; baked illumination, smeared polar regions and source resolution varying from about 0.2 to 1.6 km/pixel. Published simple cylindrical grid: west longitude 360-0 left to right. Registration is resampled to planetocentric latitude and the measured shape's longitudes: tan(published latitude) = (207.8/190.6)^2 tan(planetocentric latitude) and published longitude = longitude - 3.85 deg.
bodies.registration: Determined on 2026-10-17 by correlating the published map with synthetic shading of the Gaskell shape in 84 regions: mean correlation 0.04 as published, 0.52 after correction (83/84 regions improved); best fit k=1.190, offset -3.85 deg. The same shape matches 21 IAU gazetteer craters within a median +0.40 deg latitude and -0.34 deg longitude. The cause of the published offset is not established.
bodies.notice: Forma medida (Gaskell/Cassini) e mosaico Cassini em cores realcadas IR-verde-UV, nao cor natural. Mosaico reprojetado sobre a forma; polos com baixa definicao.

shape_source.frame: Gaskell Mimas body-fixed frame (cartographic longitudes; source W0 337.46 deg)
shape_source.credit: Gaskell, R.W. (2020). Gaskell Mimas Shape Model V1.0, urn:nasa:pds:gaskell.mimas.shape-model::1.0, NASA Planetary Data System, doi:10.26033/22n9-v553; Cassini ISS and Voyager 1 images
shape_source.limits: Q=256 vertex-facet version of the ICQ model (684 landmarks, RMS 144 m/dof per source); plate edges about 1.0-1.7 km. Original coordinates converted from km to metres without rescaling or recentring; only ICQ duplicate vertices unused by any plate are dropped. The source frame uses W0 337.46 deg while Albert orients Mimas with pck00011 (333.46 deg): surface longitudes agree with IAU gazetteer craters, but the inertial rotation phase may differ by about 4 deg.

bodies.name: Tita
bodies.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona (Cassini ISS)
bodies.limits: Global Cassini ISS mosaic at 938 nm (PIA22770, 2018): calibrated normal albedo of the surface seen through the haze in the near infrared, 16 pixels per degree. Not the visible-light appearance, which is the haze shown by default. Published grid: east longitude 0-360 left to right; registration checked against IAU gazetteer craters (Menrva, Sinlap, Selk, Ksa, Hano, Afekan) and lakes. No DEM.

haze.reference: Chromaticity of the lit disc in the Cassini ISS natural colour composite PIA06230 (red/green/violet filters, phase 56 deg), linear RGB (0.570, 0.378, 0.052), scaled to a visible geometric albedo of 0.22. The detached high haze is a translucent bluish shell at about 400 km with forward scattering; its altitude changed with season during Cassini. Approximate visual model, not radiative transfer.

bodies.notice: Luz visivel: nevoa alaranjada com cor de imagem Cassini em cor natural; a superficie so aparece em infravermelho. Opcao abaixo: superficie em 938 nm.

bodies.name: Hiperion

colour.reference: Chromaticity of the lit disc in the Cassini ISS natural colour composite PIA08240 (red/green/blue filters, 28 June 2006; sRGB decoded, pixels above 10% of the peak luminance: linear RGB (0.441, 0.367, 0.276)), scaled to a visible geometric albedo of about 0.3 (published estimates range from about 0.2 to 0.44). Source https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/psd/photojournal/pia/pia08/pia08240/PIA08240.tif, 190648 bytes, SHA-256 c2867245e4102b3096dd9ad9b23aef4ceaacf3677358974b75361bafc71139b4.

bodies.credit: Colour measured in NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute PIA08240 (Cassini ISS natural colour)
bodies.limits: No surface map: one uniform colour over the measured shape, so the real albedo contrast (dark material in crater floors) is not shown; the relief and its shading come from the plate model alone. The NASA VTAD 3D model (Hyperion_1_1000.glb) was evaluated and rejected on 2026-10-17: after the best scale/rotation/translation fit onto these plates (24 principal-axis starts, Gauss-Newton on radial residuals) its mesh matches only the overall shape (radial residual median 4.4 km, RMS 8.2 km, scale 0.896, a mirrored fit is no better), and neither its relief nor its texture correlates with the measured relief (mean 0.02-0.05 over 84 regions at 3-9 deg scales, against 0.999 in a self-test), so its craters would not fall on real ones.

orientation.reference: Hyperion rotates chaotically and pck00011 has no orientation model. Illustrative: the instantaneous spin solution for 2005 day 268 17:20 - day 269 02:18 UTC (pole RA 299.8 deg, Dec 58.7 deg, 72 deg/day; J. Bauer and P. Thomas, 'Hyperion: the sponge moon', JPL/Cornell, 28 Aug 2007, table of Cassini ISS control-point spin solutions) is held fixed, and the phase is anchored on the sub-solar point of image N1506385183 in the shape model's own frame (Table 1 of the PDS document; UTC from the spacecraft clock count, within about a minute). It reproduces the observed sub-solar latitude within 0.2 deg and longitudes over that flyby within 0.01 deg; at other dates the real orientation differs arbitrarily. scripts/anchor-orientation.py reproduces W0.

bodies.notice: Forma medida (Thomas/Cassini) com cor uniforme medida em imagem Cassini de cor natural; sem mapa de albedo. Rotacao caotica: orientacao ilustrativa, ancorada no sobrevoo de 2005.

shape_source.frame: Thomas Hyperion body-fixed frame: +Z the spin axis observed on 2005 day 268, +X the prime meridian (crater Bahloo at 196 deg W); no IAU model
shape_source.credit: Thomas, P., Joseph, J., and Ansty, T. (2018). Saturn Small Moon Shape Models V1.0, urn:nasa:pds:saturn_satellite_shape_models::1.0, NASA Planetary Data System, doi:10.26033/ewy3-jy61; Cassini ISS images
shape_source.limits: Plate model with 29,268 plates (edges about 3.4-6.0 km); origin at the model centre of figure within about 200 m. Positions on the best-imaged side (roughly 140-300 deg W near the equator) are uncertain by under 1 km, on the opposite side by up to 6 km; small craters are not reliably represented. Original coordinates converted from km to metres without rescaling or recentring.

bodies.name: Febe
bodies.credit: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute
bodies.limits: Static Cassini ISS greyscale map (PIA07775, December 2005), contrast-stretched with baked illumination; not calibrated albedo. Source resolution varies widely: large areas are smeared from low-resolution images. North of about 60 deg N (partly from 30 deg N) and south of 81 deg S are unobserved: the pack fills them (black fill, the near-black noise connected to it and a 2 px anti-aliased edge) with the local mean of the observed surroundings (about 2 deg), fading to the median grey; uniform grey patches in the south are the map authors' own fill. Published simple cylindrical grid, 8 pixels per degree: west longitude 180-0-180 left to right (east longitude -180 to 180); frame and labels cropped.
bodies.registration: Checked on 2026-10-17 by correlating the packed map with synthetic shading of the Gaskell shape in the 58 regions without gaps: mean correlation 0.109 as published. The best models of a wide scan (k 1.00-1.05, longitude +1 to +2 deg, mean up to 0.118) are not significantly better (paired test, two standard errors), so the published grid is kept; registration uncertainty is about 2 deg (4 km). Rim-crest fits of 13 IAU gazetteer craters scatter by about 5 deg (craters of 30-100 km on a 213 km body) and do not constrain it.
bodies.notice: Forma medida (Gaskell/Cassini) e mapa Cassini em tons de cinza. Sem observacao ao norte de ~60N e ao sul de 81S: cinza medio. Registro do mapa incerto em ~2 graus.

The source pole differs from pck00011 by 0.08 deg in declination; prime meridian and rotation rate are the same.

bodies.name: Nereida

colour.reference: Visible geometric albedo 0.25 +/- 0.02 (NEATM fit to Spitzer and Herschel data, Kiss et al. 2016, MNRAS, doi:10.1093/mnras/stw081; 0.24-0.29 across their models). Its spectral slope is close to the dark-neutral group of Centaurs and trans-Neptunian objects; rendered neutral.

bodies.credit: Albedo and colour after Kiss et al. (2016), Kepler/K2, Herschel and Spitzer
bodies.limits: No shape model or resolved image: Voyager 2 observed Nereid only from about 4.7 million km. Rendered as a sphere of the catalogue radius (diameter 340 km; Kiss et al. 2016 give 335-345 km, Voyager 350 +/- 50 km) with one uniform colour. Light curves allow at most a 1.3:1 elongation, so the real outline may differ by tens of kilometres.

orientation.reference: No IAU model and no measured pole. Rotation period 11.594 +/- 0.017 h from Kepler/K2 (Kiss et al. 2016); the pole is set to Neptune's pck00011 pole (without periodic terms) and the phase is arbitrary. On a uniform sphere the orientation has no visible effect.

bodies.notice: Sem forma nem imagem resolvida (Voyager 2 a 4,7 milhoes de km): esfera de 340 km com albedo e cor medidos. O alongamento real pode chegar a 1,3:1.

bodies.name: Proteu

colour.reference: Neutral: Voyager 2 colour measurements of Proteus between 0.4 and 0.6 micrometres are flat (Thomas and Veverka, 1991). Visible geometric albedo 0.096, the commonly quoted value; Voyager-era estimates without the opposition effect were about 0.06.

bodies.credit: Neutral colour after Voyager 2 photometry (Thomas and Veverka, 1991)
bodies.limits: No surface map: one uniform neutral colour over the shape model, so albedo variations and the craters Voyager 2 resolved (about 1.3 km/pixel at best) are not shown beyond the model's own 5 deg relief. Voyager imaged only part of Proteus; no public global mosaic from NASA, and no NASA 3D model, is available.
bodies.notice: Forma de Stooke (grade de raios a cada 5 graus, imagens Voyager 2) com cor neutra uniforme: sem mapa de albedo. Detalhe limitado a ~17 km.

shape_source.frame: Stooke Proteus body-fixed frame: planetocentric, west longitude, 0 deg facing Neptune (as IAU_PROTEUS); grid origin not at the centre of figure
shape_source.credit: Stooke, P. (2025). Stooke small bodies shape models V1.0, urn:nasa:pds:small_bodies.stooke.shape-models::1.0, NASA Planetary Data System, doi:10.26033/yt84-5y91; Stooke (1994), Earth, Moon and Planets 65, 31-54; Voyager 2 images
shape_source.limits: Radius every 5 deg of latitude and longitude (about 17 km at the equator) from Voyager 2 limbs and terminators, locally modified for large craters and ridges; the author notes that such models may exaggerate the depth of depressions. Volume-equivalent radius 201.0 km, against 210 +/- 7 km from Karkoschka (2003). Triangulated through the published points only (quads split into two triangles, fans at the poles); radii converted from km to metres without rescaling or recentring.

bodies.name: 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko

colour.reference: Geometric albedo 6.5 +/- 0.2% at 649 nm and disk-averaged spectral slope 11%/(100 nm) at low phase (OSIRIS, Fornasier et al. 2015, A&A 583, A30, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/201525901); channels at about 610, 550 and 465 nm from that slope. Local albedo varies by up to 16% (Hapi) and the slope reddens with phase; not shown.

bodies.credit: Colour after OSIRIS photometry (Fornasier et al. 2015)
bodies.limits: No albedo map: one uniform colour over the measured shape; the relief comes from the plate model alone. Orientation follows pck00011 (Rosetta-era pole and 12.404 h period); the spin period shortened at the 2015 and 2021 perihelia, so the rotation phase today is not a prediction. No coma or tail is drawn here.
bodies.notice: Forma medida (Rosetta/OSIRIS) com cor uniforme medida; sem mapa de albedo. Fase de rotacao atual nao prevista: o periodo mudou nas passagens de 2015 e 2021.

shape_source.credit: ESA/Rosetta/MPS for OSIRIS Team, LAM-PSI stereophotoclinometry shape model (OSPCLPS, 195k plates), DSK by N. Bachman (NAIF/JPL), ESA SPICE Service; mirror of https://spiftp.esac.esa.int/data/SPICE/ROSETTA/kernels/dsk/
shape_source.limits: Decimated version (194,668 plates, edges about 23 m) of the OSIRIS SPC model; volume-equivalent radius 1681 m against the 1650 m catalogue radius. 13 zero-thickness flaps of the decimation (a plate and its reverse, 26 plates) and the 13 vertices only they used are dropped; nothing else is changed. Original coordinates in metres, body-fixed Cheops-meridian frame and source origin; no rescaling or recentring. About 4% of plates face the origin (the neck between the lobes).
